cards.front: PPROM (preterm prelabour rupture of membranes) diagnosis: history of fluid gush + sterile speculum examination showing pooling of amniotic fluid; avoid [___] vaginal exam (raises infection risk, shortens latency).
cards.context:
The 'no digital VE in PPROM' rule is a key safety rule: each digital exam introduces vaginal flora into the cervix and through ruptured membranes, raising chorioamnionitis risk + shortening latency by hours.

Use sterile speculum instead — visualises cervix + pooling without entering the os. If labour established and you need dilatation, a single careful digital exam may be unavoidable — document the indication.

'Gush' history is sensitive but not specific (urinary incontinence, discharge, amniocentesis leak can mimic) — confirm with speculum + IGFBP-1/PAMG-1 if uncertain.

cards.front: Placental abruption is premature separation of a normally implanted placenta — diagnosed clinically; USS detects only ~[___]% of cases.
cards.context:
The diagnostic trap is concealed abruption: blood may dissect between placenta and uterine wall WITHOUT escaping through the cervix.

A patient with severe pain and a tender, 'wooden' uterus can have little or no visible vaginal bleeding, and a normal scan does not exclude abruption.

Risk factors cluster around vascular insult: prior abruption (5-15% recurrence), pre-eclampsia, smoking, cocaine, blunt trauma, IUGR, advanced age, IVF, multiparity.

cards.front: Secondary PPH (24 hours to 6 weeks postpartum) is most commonly due to retained products of conception or [___]; investigate with pelvic ultrasound.
cards.context:
Secondary PPH (24 h to 6 weeks postpartum) has different commonest causes than primary PPH (atony in the first hour).

Workup: pelvic USS for retained products (echogenic intracavity material), FBC for anaemia, βhCG to exclude gestational trophoblastic disease (persistent/rising βhCG → urgent gynae oncology).

cards.front: Australian stillbirth rate is approximately 7 per 1000 births; about [___]% are considered potentially preventable.
cards.context:
Australia's stillbirth rate (~7 per 1000) has barely moved in two decades despite gains elsewhere in maternal-fetal medicine.

The 20-week / 400g threshold (Australian/AIHW definition; WHO uses ≥28 weeks / ≥1000g for international comparison) separates stillbirth from late miscarriage.

That a fifth to a third are potentially preventable is the rationale behind the Safer Baby Bundle — the flat rate reflects missed modifiable risks (FGR, smoking, supine sleep), not an unavoidable floor.

cards.front: The commonest cause of primary postpartum haemorrhage is uterine [___] (poor tone).
cards.context: Of the 4 Ts (Tone, Trauma, Tissue, Thrombin), uterine atony is by far the commonest cause of primary PPH — which is why first-line management is to rub up a contraction and give uterotonics.

cards.front: [___] uterus is blood infiltration of the myometrium from severe placental abruption, causing uterine atony and PPH; risk of DIC from disrupted decidua.
cards.context:
Couvelaire uterus (uteroplacental apoplexy) is the visual signature of severe placental abruption at caesarean — blood has dissected from retroplacental haematoma into myometrium, producing a purple, bruised uterus.

Severe abruption also releases tissue factor + procoagulants from disrupted decidua → DIC (consumptive coagulopathy: falling platelets, falling fibrinogen, raised D-dimer, prolonged INR/APTT).

Hysterectomy may be unavoidable if uterotonics, B-Lynch, UAE all fail.

cards.front: The single biggest risk factor for postpartum endometritis is route of birth: [___]; treatment is amoxicillin + gentamicin + metronidazole.
cards.context:
Endometritis is polymicrobial bacterial infection of the endometrium + adjacent decidua.

Presentation: fever ≥38°C, lower abdominal/uterine tenderness, malodorous lochia, raised WCC.

Consider differentials (wound infection, retained products, septic pelvic thrombophlebitis).

cards.front: Neonatal hypoglycaemia: BGL <[___] mmol/L; at-risk groups (LGA, IDM, SGA, preterm) need BGL check at 1-2 hours; symptomatic → IV dextrose 10%.
cards.context:
Neonatal hypoglycaemia (BGL <2.6 mmol/L) is the commonest metabolic problem in newborns.

Screen at-risk infants: BGL at 1-2 h then before feeds for ≥12-24 h.

cards.front: cystic fibrosis (IRT marker) has been part of Australian newborn screening since the 1980s-90s; the genuinely recent additions are SMA (SMN1 deletion — gene therapy is disease-modifying) and [___] (TREC assay — early stem cell transplant).
cards.context:
CF (~1:2500) has been part of the Australian newborn screening panel since the 1980s-90s: raised IRT → DNA test for CFTR mutations; early dx enables prophylactic enzyme replacement, salt supplementation, surveillance.

SMA and SCID are the genuinely recent additions to the panel.

SMA (~1:10,000): SMN1 deletion by PCR; presymptomatic gene therapy (onasemnogene) is disease-modifying and most effective when given before symptom onset, not a guaranteed cure.

cards.front: The 0–10 score assessed at 1 and 5 minutes to summarise a newborn's condition is the [___] score.
cards.context: A 0–10 snapshot of newborn condition at 1 and 5 minutes (Appearance, Pulse, Grimace, Activity, Respiration). It describes the baby — it does NOT guide resuscitation, which proceeds on breathing/heart rate in real time.

cards.front: A low-lying placenta has its edge within [___] mm of the internal os without covering it; seen in ~5% at the second-trimester scan but only 0.5-1% remain low-lying at term as ~85% resolve.
cards.context:
Low-lying placenta: placental edge within 20 mm of the internal cervical os but NOT covering it — found in ~5% of pregnancies at the second-trimester scan.

~85% resolve to a normal position by term as the lower segment develops, leaving only ~0.5-1% still low-lying at term. Placenta praevia: placenta covers or overlies the internal cervical os.

Unlike a low-lying placenta, true praevia seen at the second-trimester scan resolves far less reliably and should not be assumed to migrate away.

cards.front: Antenatal betamethasone for preterm birth: total dose 22.8 mg given between 23+0 and [___]+6 weeks; reduces respiratory distress syndrome, intraventricular haemorrhage, and neonatal death.
cards.context:
Antenatal corticosteroids accelerate fetal type II pneumocyte maturation, surfactant production + release. Benefit largest 24-48 h after first dose, peaks at 48 h, persists ~7 days.

Betamethasone preferred over dexamethasone (longer placental half-life).

Standard (Celestone Chronodose, Australian/RANZCOG-aligned protocol): 11.4 mg IM ×2 24 h apart (total 22.8 mg); indicated 23+0 to 34+6 weeks when delivery anticipated within 7 days.

cards.front: Universal (rather than ethnicity-based) core reproductive carrier screening covers [___], SMA, and fragile X.
cards.context:
Most affected children are born to couples without a family history, and self-reported ethnicity poorly predicts carrier status. RANZCOG therefore recommends offering screening regardless of background.

The core panel covers three conditions; expanded screens cover many more. If both partners are carriers, options can include PGT-M with IVF, donor gametes or prenatal diagnosis.

cards.front: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) risk assessment is mandatory at [___], on admission to labour ward, and postpartum; prophylaxis decisions follow a validated phase-specific tool.
cards.context:
Assess obstetric VTE risk at booking, admission to labour ward and postpartum. Use a named, validated tool with phase-specific thresholds.

Previous VTE and thrombophilia follow separate pathways; document the score and follow the local protocol.

Prophylaxis dose and duration depend on indication, weight, renal function and risk phase; extend postpartum prophylaxis for high-risk patients.

cards.front: In healthy term infants, cord clamping is typically delayed for at least [___] seconds; this increases neonatal iron stores and reduces anaemia at 4-6 months.
cards.context:
Delayed cord clamping (≥60 sec, often 1-3 min) allows ~80-100 mL of placental-to-neonatal transfusion — boosting blood volume ~25%, raising iron stores, reducing anaemia at 4-6 months.

Cochrane backs it as standard for healthy term and preterm babies; the old 'clamp and cut immediately' is now wrong.

Immediate clamping is still preferred for severe maternal haemorrhage or when the neonate needs immediate resuscitation (unless 'resuscitation with cord intact' is possible).

cards.front: Newborn metabolic screening includes [___] (preventable intellectual disability with diet) and MCAD deficiency (hypoketotic hypoglycaemia, prevent fasting).
cards.context:
Two metabolic conditions on the Guthrie panel: phenylketonuria (PKU), where diet prevents phenylalanine neurotoxicity, and MCAD deficiency, where avoiding fasting prevents hypoketotic hypoglycaemia.

MCAD (~1:15,000) impairs fatty acid oxidation, so patients can't generate ketones during fasting/illness — presents with hypoketotic hypoglycaemia.

cards.front: Chorionicity must be determined by ultrasound (USS) at 11–14 weeks. Lambda sign = [___]; T sign = monochorionic.
cards.context:
Chorionicity means placental sharing, and it drives twin-pregnancy risk more than zygosity. It is best assigned on first-trimester ultrasound scan (USS), before the inter-twin membrane becomes harder to interpret.

Lambda/twin-peak sign means dichorionic twins with placental tissue between membranes. T sign means monochorionic twins, who need closer surveillance for twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome.

cards.front: Hypertension in pregnancy is SBP ≥140 and/or DBP ≥90 mmHg on [___] occasions ≥4 h apart (or a single reading ≥160/110).
cards.context:
The pregnancy threshold (140/90) sits below the general adult treatment threshold because mild hypertension matters more here.

Placental perfusion is pressure-dependent, and untreated HTN drives pre-eclampsia, abruption, and IUGR.

Timing reframes the same number. Before 20 weeks, 140/90 is chronic HTN (secondary-cause workup); after 20 weeks it is gestational HTN or pre-eclampsia, triggering an end-organ screen (urinalysis, LFTs, FBC, creatinine).
